name: Geddes Plaza
summary: Geddes Plaza in Solvay, New York is a community shopping center anchored by Priscilla's Save the Animals Thrift Shop, a volunteer-run charitable store supporting animal rescue efforts in Syracuse. The plaza serves as a neighborhood destination for value-conscious shoppers seeking unique finds while supporting a worthy cause.
demographics: Geddes Plaza serves a diverse, community-oriented demographic in the Syracuse area, particularly drawing value-conscious shoppers and animal lovers from middle-income households. The center attracts families and retirees who appreciate local, mission-driven businesses and thrift shopping opportunities. Visitors tend to be socially conscious consumers interested in supporting animal welfare causes while finding affordable household goods, collectibles, and furniture. The trade area encompasses the Solvay neighborhood and surrounding Syracuse communities, with shoppers seeking both bargain hunting experiences and opportunities to contribute to local charitable causes.
description: Geddes Plaza is a community-focused shopping center located at 527 Charles Avenue in Solvay, New York, serving the greater Syracuse area. The plaza is perhaps best known as the home of Priscilla's Save the Animals Thrift Shop, a volunteer-run charitable organization dedicated to rescuing stray and injured animals and finding them forever homes. This unique thrift shop, located in the far right corner of the plaza, operates Friday through Sunday and offers an ever-changing selection of housewares, collectibles, books, jewelry, linens, furniture, craft supplies, and seasonal décor. All proceeds from purchases directly support animal welfare efforts in Syracuse, including pet food, medical supplies, spay and neuter services, and veterinary bills for animals in need. The center provides essential services to the community while fostering a spirit of volunteerism and compassion, making it a beloved destination for both bargain hunters and animal advocates throughout the Syracuse region.
